text: Right, time for some sporting history. Scott Pendlebury has officially broken the all-time VFL-AFL games record, playing his 433rd match for Collingwood. That's more games than any player in the 129-year history of the competition, breaking Brent Harvey's record that stood since 2016.

speaker: alice
text: What makes this even more special is that Pendlebury was apparently a surprise early pick when the Pies drafted him. Now he's not just broken the record but he's still playing at an elite level at 36 years old. The bloke's been a one-club player his entire career, which is pretty rare in modern footy.

speaker: charlie
text: And let's be honest, seeing players stay loyal to one club for their entire career gives you a bit of faith in the game, doesn't it. In an age where everyone's chasing bigger contracts and better opportunities, Pendlebury's shown you can build something special by staying put and growing with your team. That's 433 games of commitment right there.
